title: Nanjing Yunjin intelligent question-answering system based on knowledge graphs and retrieval augmented generation technology
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily a domain-specific application (cultural heritage Q&A) that uses FAISS as a storage and retrieval tool within a RAG pipeline; vector databases are not the subject of analysis, comparison, or improvement.
research_focus: Design and implementation of an intelligent question-answering system for Nanjing Yunjin (traditional Chinese silk weaving) cultural heritage that integrates Knowledge Graphs with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to overcome limitations of KG-only Q&A systems.
method: The system uses ROBERTA to vectorize Nanjing Yunjin textual data, stores vectors in a FAISS database (indexFlatL2 with Euclidean distance) for approximate nearest neighbor retrieval, and feeds retrieved results into the LLAMA large language model for augmented generation of answers. A Knowledge Graph module handles queries matching predefined entities and relationships, while the RAG module handles queries outside the KG.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; ROBERTA; LLAMA; m3e-base; bge-large; bert-large
application_domain: Cultural heritage (Nanjing Yunjin silk weaving) question-answering and knowledge retrieval
results_summary: The paper builds and implements a Q&A system combining Knowledge Graphs and RAG for Nanjing Yunjin cultural knowledge. Experiments comparing ROBERTA, m3e-base, bge-large, and bert-large for vectorization showed that roberta-large achieved 99.82% similarity in the FAISS retrieval stage, outperforming the other models. The FAISS database with indexFlatL2 index and cosine similarity was used to retrieve top-k most similar results for query matching. The system was implemented in an MVC architecture and demonstrated improved handling of polysemy, vague language, and sentence ambiguity compared to the previous KG-only system. The authors conclude the system provides a paradigm for building Q&A systems for other intangible cultural heritages.
limitations: Knowledge graphs require constant updating and rely on predefined entity and relationship types; KG-based retrieval struggles with ambiguous or complex natural language queries; Traditional KGs lack deep reasoning and inferential abilities for complex questions; KGs can only answer questions related to entities and relationships already modeled in the graph
research_gaps: Further exploration and discovery of the knowledge structure of human intangible heritage; Extending the paradigm to other intangible cultural heritages

title: A fine-tuning enhanced RAG system with quantized influence measure as AI judge
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about RAG system design, LLM fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA), and chatbot application in homeless shelters. Vector databases are used as a component (chroma library) for storing embeddings but are not the subject of analysis, comparison, or improvement.
research_focus: Enhancing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems by integrating fine-tuned LLMs (Llama2 via LoRA/QLoRA) with vector databases, and introducing a Quantized Influence Measure (QIM) as an AI Judge for result selection, applied to a homeless shelter communication chatbot.
method: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Llama2 using LoRA and QLoRA with sequential hyperparameter tuning (dropout, alpha, rank), integration with a vector database (chroma) for retrieval, and a QIM-based AI Judge mechanism for filtering retrieved results. Evaluated against baselines (Davinci002, Llama2, Langchain+SerpAPI) over seven trials.
mentioned_systems: chroma; Langchain; SerpAPI; Llama2; Davinci002; Hugging Face; huggify-data
application_domain: Homeless shelter communication and social services chatbot (Youth Spirit Artworks Tiny House Empowerment Village)
results_summary: The paper evaluates a fine-tuning enhanced RAG system with QIM against several baselines for chatbot creation. The RAG (L) model (RAG + fine-tuned Llama2) achieved the highest average score of 0.934 with a standard deviation of 0.016, outperforming Davinci002 (0.737) and standalone Llama2 (0.871). The RAG (L+QIM) configuration with the AI Judge further improved the average score to 0.950. Fine-tuning with LoRA/QLoRA achieved a 69% reduction in loss (from 0.32 to 0.1) over 10 epochs. The results demonstrate that combining fine-tuned LLMs with vector database retrieval and QIM-based filtering yields superior and more consistent performance for domain-specific chatbot applications.
research_gaps: Extending the framework to other vulnerable populations (low-income families, refugees, disaster-stricken areas); Integrating the system with healthcare and social services for medical and mental health information; Exploring scalability to a global context including multiple languages and cultural nuances

title: Facial image recognition for biometric authentication systems using a combination of geometrical feature points and low-level visual features
relevance_reason: The paper is about facial recognition for biometric authentication; the 'feature vector database' is merely a storage mechanism for feature matrices, and no modern vector database system, indexing method, or similarity search technology is discussed.
research_focus: Biometric facial image recognition by combining geometrical feature points (via Active Shape Model) and low-level visual features (colour and texture) for authentication purposes.
method: Multivariate correlation analysis: geometrical features extracted with Active Shape Model, colour features from YCbCr model, texture features via autocorrelation; features stored as a tensor matrix in a feature vector database and compared using the Canonical Correlation method at varying significance levels.
application_domain: Biometric authentication / facial recognition
results_summary: The paper proposes a facial recognition method that combines geometrical features (Active Shape Model) with low-level visual features (YCbCr colour, autocorrelation texture) and compares them via Canonical Correlation against a stored feature vector database. Experiments on GT, LFW, Pointing '04, and a custom celebrity dataset yielded mean precision scores of 95.27%, 94.20%, 96.19%, and 96.05% respectively. The optimal significance level was determined to be 15%, producing a mP@a of 98.17%. F-scores ranged from 95.15% to 97.08% across datasets. The results were found to be comparable to existing methods such as KPM and CRRF.

title: Using text embedding models as text classifiers with medical data

mentioned_systems: Pinecone; text-embedding-ada-002; text-embedding-gecko@001; gpt-3.5-turbo; flan-t5-xl; LLaMA-70b-chat; Med-PaLM; Vertex AI
application_domain: Medical text classification (NLP applied to clinical/medical data)
results_summary: The paper tested a pipeline of text embedding models and a vector database (Pinecone) for classifying medical text across 8 ailments. mentioned_systems: Qdrant; Pinecone; Weaviate; Milvus; Gemini-2.0-flash; Gemini-2.0-flash-lite; Mistral-saba-24b; Gemma2-9b-it; bge-small-en-v1.5; bge-base-en-v1.5; bge-large-en-v1.5
application_domain: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for internal company knowledge, specifically applied to long-form biographical text data
results_summary: The paper conducted 48 experiments varying vector embedding models, chunk sizes, and LLM selections on a biographical dataset stored in Qdrant. research_focus: Design and implementation of a medical chatbot that provides context-aware information on symptoms, medications, and health tips using a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline combining a large language model with vector-based semantic retrieval.
method: A RAG pipeline where medical reference documents (GALE Encyclopedia of Medicine) are segmented into text chunks, converted to vector embeddings, and stored in the Pinecone vector database for semantic similarity search. The LLaMA-2 architecture is used as the language model, deployed locally via LlamaCpp, with LangChain orchestrating the retrieval-generation interaction. The system is built as a Django web application supporting multi-session conversations.
application_domain: Medical information retrieval and healthcare chatbot
results_summary: The paper presents a complete medical chatbot system that combines Pinecone-based vector retrieval with a locally hosted LLaMA-2 model to answer medical queries. The GALE Encyclopedia of Medicine (637 pages) is segmented and embedded for semantic search. Experimental results show the chatbot delivers reliable and contextually appropriate medical responses with moderately good response times on CPU-based infrastructure. The authors conclude that integrating Pinecone-based vector retrieval with LLMs offers an effective and privacy-conscious approach to delivering healthcare information. The system supports multi-session conversations and chat history for continuity.
limitations: Difficulty dealing with complicated medical cases; Data quality concerns in the medical reference dataset; Lack of real-time medical information updates; Performance constrained by CPU-based infrastructure; No multi-language support
research_gaps: Real-time information updates for medical knowledge; Multi-language support for the chatbot; Handling complicated medical cases more effectively; Improving data quality of the medical reference source

title: Retrieval-grounded multilingual LLM assistance for island smallholder farmers
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about designing and deploying an LLM-based agricultural assistant, and vector databases are only mentioned in passing as an alternative grounding approach (vector-store RAG) that the authors deliberately chose not to use in favour of tool-augmented retrieval.
research_focus: Design, implementation, and deployment of a multilingual, geospatially grounded LLM conversational assistant (Falco eleonorae) for smallholder farmers on Greek islands, using tool-augmented retrieval via Model Context Protocol as an alternative to vector-store RAG for grounding in small, curated local knowledge.
method: A thin Backend-for-Frontend proxy architecture in front of a managed agronomic agent (Jackdaw), with grounding realised through a Model Context Protocol tool querying a read-only bilingual data API wrapped in a geospatial Well-Known Text envelope, combined with multimodal interaction (text, voice via Amazon Transcribe, image via Claude Sonnet 4.5) and answer generation via OpenAI gpt-5nano/gpt-5-mini.
mentioned_systems: Falco eleonorae; Jackdaw; OpenAI gpt-5nano; OpenAI gpt-5-mini; Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5; Amazon Transcribe; Model Context Protocol (MCP); PoliRURAL Plus platform
application_domain: Agricultural extension and agronomic advisory for smallholder farmers
results_summary: The paper reports the implementation and deployment of the Falco eleonorae assistant as an engineering artefact for the Kythera and Antikythera pilot under the PoliRURAL Plus initiative. It describes the four-layer system architecture, the tool-augmented retrieval grounding mechanism, the multimodal conversational interface, and the security and data-protection design. No controlled user study or formal quantitative evaluation was conducted; the reported latency figures are anecdotal observations. The paper positions tool-augmented retrieval over a curated data API as a deliberate alternative to vector-store RAG for small, structured, frequently edited local knowledge. The design is offered as a transferable pattern for other remote, resource-constrained rural communities.
limitations: No formal evaluation or controlled user study has been conducted; quantitative validation of answer quality, grounding faithfulness, latency, and user satisfaction is pending; Dependence on external upstream services with no local fallback model if the upstream agent is unavailable; Upstream geospatial services observed to be unreliable during integration; end-to-end grounding may not be fully active in production at all times; Stopgap authentication via credential reuse instead of a registered OAuth2 flow, which is fragile; Image understanding is limited to short descriptions folded into text and is not a diagnostic system; Closed-source proprietary dependencies (OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon) constrain reproducibility to the architectural level
research_gaps: Structured field evaluation with the pilot cohort measuring grounding faithfulness, answer quality in Greek, latency, and user-reported usefulness; Replacing stopgap authentication with a registered OAuth2 client; Hardening the dependence on upstream services; Expanding the curated local knowledge exposed through the grounding tools

title: AI Study Assistant Using Vector Database and Large Language Models for Intelligent Question Answering from PDF Documents
relevance_reason: The vector database is used solely as a storage and retrieval component within a RAG pipeline for an educational application; the paper does not analyze, compare, benchmark, or propose improvements to vector database technology or its core indexing/similarity search mechanisms.
research_focus: An AI Study Assistant that uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework combining vector databases and Large Language Models to enable intelligent question answering from uploaded PDF documents in an educational context.
method: PDF documents are processed and converted into semantic embeddings, stored in a vector database. User queries trigger similarity search to retrieve relevant document sections, which are then passed to an integrated LLM to generate context-aware responses.
application_domain: Education – intelligent question answering from academic PDF documents
results_summary: The paper presents a RAG-based AI Study Assistant that combines document processing, embedding generation, vector similarity search, and LLM-based response generation. The developed system successfully performs PDF-based question answering and context-aware information retrieval. The approach is reported to help students reduce manual searching time, improve knowledge understanding, and achieve personalized learning experiences. No quantitative benchmarks or comparisons with alternative systems are provided.
limitations: Performance depends on the quality of the LLM

title: Architecting a Low-Latency RAG System for Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) Customer Support: A Case Study in Industrial Software Deployment
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about RAG system architecture and low-latency LLM deployment for FMCG customer support; Pinecone is used as a vector indexing tool within the pipeline but is not analyzed, compared, or studied in depth as a vector database system.
research_focus: Design and evaluation of a low-latency Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) customer support, balancing response accuracy with system latency in an industrial deployment setting.
method: The authors designed and implemented a RAG pipeline integrating document ingestion, vector-based retrieval using Pinecone, and LLM inference via Groq's infrastructure. They empirically evaluated response accuracy and end-to-end latency using 50 domain-specific customer support queries, comparing a local GPU-based deployment against a Groq-based deployment.
application_domain: FMCG customer support (product specifications, ingredients, usage instructions, company procedures)
results_summary: The proposed RAG system achieved an overall response accuracy of 72.0% across 50 FMCG customer support queries, demonstrating that retrieval-based grounding can improve response consistency with organizational product information. The Groq-based deployment significantly reduced latency compared to the local GPU deployment: TTFT dropped from 742 ms to 118 ms, end-to-end latency from 2847 ms to 1246 ms, and token throughput increased from 42.8 to 305.9 tokens per second. Most incorrect responses were attributed to incomplete retrieval results, ambiguity in product descriptions, or failure to fully incorporate retrieved context into the generated response. The authors conclude that low-latency inference infrastructure can support responsive customer support interactions while maintaining retrieval-grounded generation, though the results are limited to a single-brand, small-scale evaluation.
limitations: Evaluation dataset consisted of only 50 question-answer pairs from a single FMCG brand, limiting generalizability; Response quality assessed through manual evaluation without multiple independent annotators or inter-rater reliability measurement; Insufficient dataset size to support meaningful statistical significance testing; Retrieval component uses a lightweight hash-based vector representation capturing only lexical similarity rather than deep semantic relationships; No dedicated retrieval effectiveness metrics (Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR, context coverage) were evaluated; No controlled ablation experiments to isolate contributions of retrieval configuration, prompt design, serving infrastructure, and inference hardware; Scalability under concurrent user workloads and larger knowledge base sizes was not investigated
research_gaps: Expand evaluation benchmark and incorporate multiple independent annotators to improve reliability and generalizability; Perform systematic ablation studies to understand the relative impact of each component on overall system performance; Investigate scalability under concurrent user workloads and larger knowledge base sizes; Evaluate alternative deployment frameworks such as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM; Explore transformer-based embedding models to improve retrieval quality; Investigate hybrid retrieval strategies and reranking techniques; Evaluate retrieval effectiveness using dedicated metrics such as Recall@K, Precision@K, and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)

title: AI-Driven RAG Chatbot: Combining Information Retrieval with Generative AI
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about building a RAG chatbot application for e-learning; Chroma is mentioned only as a storage tool for embeddings without any discussion of vector database internals, indexing methods, or similarity search algorithms.
research_focus: Building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot as an e-learning assistant for the subject of Artificial Intelligence, retrieving content from PDF documents to generate accurate responses to user queries.
method: PDFs are loaded, split into sections, and processed using LangChain. Embeddings are generated with Google's AI models and stored in Chroma. User queries trigger a similarity search, and Google Gemini-1.5-Pro generates a response based on the retrieved content. Flask and React are used for backend and frontend respectively.
mentioned_systems: Chroma; LangChain; Google Gemini-1.5-Pro; Flask; React; ChatGPT
application_domain: E-learning / education (specifically the subject of Artificial Intelligence)
results_summary: The paper describes the design and implementation of a RAG chatbot that processes PDF documents about Artificial Intelligence, stores embeddings in Chroma, and uses Google Gemini-1.5-Pro to generate context-specific responses. The results section presents the user interface built with React and Bootstrap. The authors claim the system delivers more accurate, domain-specific answers compared to general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT by relying on specific retrieved content rather than broad AI knowledge. The paper positions the solution as scalable and adaptable for education and other knowledge-based fields.
research_gaps: The approach can be extended to other areas such as restaurant websites or sales sites for customer question answering; As AI improves, these systems will become more personalized and efficient

title: Generative AI at the heart of the concerns of the renewable energy sector in Morocco: Development of AI assistants and analysis between vector database and rag using knowledge graph
relevance_reason: The vector database is used as one component of a RAG pipeline and compared against a knowledge graph approach, but the paper's main subject is building a domain-specific AI assistant for Morocco's energy sector, not analyzing vector database technology, indexing methods, or database performance in depth.
research_focus: Comparison of two RAG-based AI assistant approaches (vector database vs. knowledge graph) for answering domain-specific questions about Morocco's renewable energy sector.
method: Two AI assistants were developed: one using RAG with a vector database and another using RAG with a knowledge graph (LightRAG). Both were fed the same dataset (government renewable energy strategies and the 2021 development model report) and their responses to a set of questions were evaluated using BERTScore and ROUGE-L metrics.
application_domain: Renewable energy sector in Morocco, specifically answering questions about government energy strategies and policy documents.
results_summary: The paper developed and compared two RAG-based AI assistants for the Moroccan renewable energy domain. The vector database approach achieved a BERTScore of around 60% and ROUGE-L of around 5.7%, indicating limited semantic similarity and weak text correspondence with reference answers. The knowledge graph approach achieved a BERTScore of around 89% and ROUGE-L of around 70%, showing strong correlation and word-level correspondence with reference documents. The vector database failed to answer a question requiring high specificity due to its embedding-based similarity approach struggling with intricate concept relationships. The authors conclude that the knowledge graph approach is more suitable for complex, specialized domain queries.
limitations: The vector database's embedding-based similarity approach struggles to identify intricate relationships between concepts; The vector database does not guarantee comprehensive coverage of necessary information; The vector database may lack accuracy for specialized topics; The vector database was unable to answer a question requiring a high level of specificity
research_gaps: Developing an AI agent in the energy field that can automate specific tasks; Integrating the system into a multi-agent system for data analysis and optimization of decision-making processes

title: Legal Literacy in Indonesia: Leveraging Semantic-Based AI and NLP for Enhanced Civil Law Access
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about building and evaluating a legal information retrieval application for Indonesian civil law; QDrant is used solely as a vector storage tool without any in-depth analysis, comparison, or evaluation of vector database technology or indexing methods.
research_focus: Developing a semantic-based AI system (CerdasHukum) using IndoSBERT embeddings and QDrant vector storage to improve access to Indonesian civil law information for users with low legal literacy.
method: Transforming 2,074 articles from the Indonesian Civil Code into 256-dimensional semantic vectors using IndoSBERT, storing them in QDrant, and using cosine similarity to match user queries with relevant legal articles. Performance was evaluated through expert-validated recommendation accuracy and System Usability Scale (SUS) scoring.
mentioned_systems: QDrant; IndoSBERT; IndoNLU; Sentence-BERT; IndoBERT; multilingual BERT; XLM-R
application_domain: Legal information retrieval (Indonesian civil law / KUHPerdata)
results_summary: The CerdasHukum system achieved a recommendation accuracy of 76.66% validated by legal experts when matching user queries to relevant articles from the Indonesian Civil Code. Usability measured via SUS scored 74.81 (Grade B), indicating good user-friendliness. The combination of domain-specific IndoSBERT embeddings with QDrant vector storage proved effective for contextually relevant legal retrieval. The authors note that IndoSBERT outperforms general multilingual models like XLM-R for this specialized legal domain task.
research_gaps: Incorporating additional legal texts beyond the Indonesian Civil Code; Refining IndoSBERT with further domain-specific fine-tuning; Exploring multilingual embeddings or zero-shot learning for cross-border legal research; Expanding the system to other legal domains such as criminal or administrative law

title: Retrieval augmented generation with LLMs for enterprise proposal automation
relevance_reason: The vector database is used solely as a retrieval component within a RAG pipeline for enterprise proposal writing; the paper does not propose, analyze, benchmark, or discuss vector database technology, indexing methods, or system comparisons in any depth.
research_focus: Automating enterprise proposal writing (RFP responses) using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline that combines document processing, semantic vector retrieval, and LLM inference to reduce hallucinations and improve contextual grounding.
method: Documents are extracted, chunked into semantically meaningful segments, converted to dense vectors, and stored in a vector database. At query time, similarity-based retrieval fetches relevant fragments which are inserted into a structured prompt for LLM generation. The system is evaluated with an API-based LLM and a local TinyLlama model, comparing RAG-augmented vs. standalone LLM output.
application_domain: Enterprise business document generation (RFP proposal drafting)
results_summary: The paper demonstrates a RAG pipeline for enterprise proposal automation and compares it against standalone LLM generation. The standalone LLM produced fluent but hallucinatory text with approximately 40% baseless assumptions. The RAG + API-based LLM configuration achieved the highest relevance scores and significantly reduced hallucinated claims. The RAG + TinyLlama configuration showed moderate relevance with some linguistic regression and incomplete requirement coverage due to model size and context window constraints. Overall, retrieval-augmented generation improved factual accuracy and contextual grounding over blind text generation.
limitations: TinyLlama exhibited small-scale linguistic regression and incomplete coverage of requirements due to model size and context window limitations; Standalone LLM generation produced generalized statements and baseless assumptions at approximately 40% of outputs

title: Implementation of an Academic Information Chatbot Based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Using LLaMA 3.1
relevance_reason: The paper is a domain application that builds a RAG chatbot for university information; ChromaDB is mentioned only as one component of the system stack and is not analyzed, compared, or discussed in any depth regarding its indexing or search capabilities.
research_focus: Development of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based academic information chatbot integrated with the Informatics Study Program website at Muhammadiyah University of Sidoarjo, using LLaMA 3.1 via Groq API.
method: The system was built using the LangGraph architecture with ChromaDB as the vector database and LLaMA 3.1 accessed through the Groq API. Data was preprocessed and vectorized from structured JSON sources. Evaluation used the RAGAS framework for answer quality (Context Precision, Faithfulness) and load testing for system performance.
mentioned_systems: ChromaDB; LangGraph; LLaMA 3.1; Groq API; RAGAS
application_domain: Academic information retrieval and question-answering for a university study program website
results_summary: The paper developed a RAG-based chatbot integrated with a university study program website to provide fast and accurate academic information. Using the RAGAS framework, the system achieved a Context Precision score of 0.86 and a Faithfulness score of 0.77, indicating high relevance and accuracy of generated answers. Load testing via the Groq API yielded an average response latency of 2.11 seconds with a 94% success rate. The authors conclude that the RAG-based chatbot effectively overcomes the limitations of a static website in delivering contextual academic information.
research_gaps: Use of ROUGE as an evaluation metric is mismatched with question-answering tasks since ROUGE was designed for text summarization; Prior RAG chatbot implementations rely on third-party platforms or separate applications rather than direct integration with the official university website; Response latency and system efficiency remain challenges, especially when using proprietary LLMs with high cost and response time
